risks: Backend promotion remains blocked until a current-contract board AXI/DDR promotion certificate exists; this is a required later-stage gate, not a current Stage 6 static-contract failure.

If board discovery finds multiple plausible tops, wrappers, block designs, clocks, resets, AXI interfaces, or DDR address spaces, selecting one without cited evidence would contaminate every later board and backend result.
The zero clock target can cause clock/reset or runtime mismatch if generic defaults are substituted instead of binding the exact sample-project facts.

Static address-map and stream-order availability cannot establish dynamic protocol correctness. Burst crossing, beat packing, response handling, backpressure, ordering, transfer-count, or liveness faults may only appear in the canonical board-wrapped simulation.

A bit-correct DDR image roundtrip can still be insufficient if the DUT did not read every required Transformer-block weight. Complete access coverage must be joined with tensor-to-range hashes and loader/harness identity.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model outputs, tolerance, testbench, memory layout, runtime ABI, or exact wrapper source hashes during repair would invalidate comparison evidence and require a new canonical run identity.

A third-layer failure may expose a contradictory lower-layer boundary trace. Such evidence must trigger a targeted backtrack to the earliest causal layer; it must not be patched only in the board wrapper or used to skip the operator and single-layer repair order.
Adding embedding, final norm, LM head, logits, or sampling data to the board golden or complete-weight requirement would create a scope mismatch with the Transformer-block-only accelerator contract.

Evidence contamination risk: independently rerunning order, count, or deadlock checks could mix different wrapper, stimulus, checkpoint, RTL, or trace identities. Every classifier must reject evidence whose canonical run digest differs.
Data-order and shape risk: expected beat counts or logical block order derived from a different sequence bound, lane mapping, transfer unit, or block count can create false passes or false failures.
Flow-control risk: counting valid cycles instead of valid-and-ready fires can hide duplicated transfers, overcount backpressured beats, and misclassify progress.

Liveness risk: an unfrozen or wall-clock-based watchdog can classify legal compute or memory latency as deadlock, while a watchdog that treats counter toggles unrelated to accepted work as progress can conceal a real wait cycle.
Implementation/deployment risk: instrumentation attached only to a disconnected kernel or simplified wrapper would not observe board-wrapper backpressure and cannot support board-system acceptance.

Memory/runtime ownership risk: a no-progress root at the wrapper, AXI, or DDR boundary must be handed to the corresponding interface owner with correlated traces; it must not be labeled pipeline-local without an earliest causal pipeline boundary.

Lower-layer consistency risk: a board trace may contradict reusable single-layer evidence, but reopening layer 2 requires a bound earliest-violation trace. A third-layer symptom alone is insufficient for direct lower-layer repair.

Numeric-policy risk: order and liveness reports from one run must not be combined with value comparison from another run or with a changed tolerance. Checkpoint, stimulus, reference, tolerance, semantic testbench, and wrapper hashes remain immutable during repair.

Scope risk: including embedding, final norm, logits, or sampling traffic in transfer counts, weight coverage, or golden comparison would contaminate the Transformer-block accelerator acceptance boundary.

Conditional handoff risk: although the current artifact contract passed, omitting explicit canonical subviews for transfer_count_check and deadlock_watchdog could allow a downstream implementation to substitute local evidence unless the proposed refinement is materialized and audited.

Stage 7 promotion is blocked until real tool evidence produces a current-contract-valid operator-leaf promotion certificate; artifact presence or compile success cannot substitute for this certificate.

If case_operator_leaf_semantic_evidence remains encoded as a prerequisite on each leaf rather than as the downstream aggregate, an implementation could create a circular or self-satisfying evidence interpretation.

A complete checkpoint manifest without executed per-tensor loader/read evidence could falsely imply DUT weight consumption. The risk is highest for the attention and projection leaves, while weightless leaves require explicit zero-weight declarations.
An unresolved tolerance triplet before simulation would make golden comparison non-reproducible. Any tolerance selected from DUT behavior or loosened during repair would contaminate the loop.
Incorrect lane order, cast placement, residual-path alignment, causal masking, RoPE indexing, or GQA head grouping can pass structural compilation while producing semantically wrong values.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, tolerance, numeric policy, semantic-testbench contract, or boundary-contract identity during a repair would invalidate prior evidence and require a new semantic run identity rather than continuation of the same loop.

Broad replay after a localized leaf failure could reopen unrelated stages and obscure the earliest causal violation. Replay must remain limited to the implicated leaf and directly connected boundary unless contradictory bound trace evidence justifies a targeted backtrack.

A missing or broken target-model/reference checker is a verification-capability failure, not evidence of hardware correctness or incorrectness; hardware repair must not begin until the reference path is valid.
Current layer-2 blocker: artifact.stage7.operator_leaf_promotion_certificate is absent or stale for the current contract, so the connected-layer run cannot rely on reusable lower-layer closure yet.
Current layer-2 blocker: artifact.stage7.single_layer_promotion_certificate is absent, and every required single-layer execution node is still marked required_pending_execution.

A branch-identity error could feed norm1 output or a reordered stream into residual_add_1 instead of the original x stream, or feed different n2 transactions into gate and up projections. Static module presence would not detect these failures.
A residual latency or FIFO mismatch could pair attention or MLP output with the wrong tx_id, tile_id, logical index, token, or lane while preserving apparently legal valid/ready behavior.

A GQA mapping, RoPE position, causal-mask, bounded-cache-state, or sequence-length mismatch could produce numerically plausible but model-inconsistent outputs unless the target-model reference and DUT share immutable boundary metadata.
A target-activation or gate/up multiplication-order mismatch at stage_06_activation_mul could survive independent projection checks and first appear only at the connected MLP merge.
A manifest-only weight claim could conceal omitted, defaulted, sampled, misaddressed, or unread tensors. Promotion requires complete catalog coverage plus executed DUT consumption evidence.
The single_transformer_layer versus case_single_transformer_layer naming distinction could create split evidence unless an explicit alias and common source/run hash are certified.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, reference output, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench, or boundary contract after a failure would contaminate the repair loop and invalidate comparison evidence.
Reopening an independently passed leaf without a connected-layer trace identifying the earliest contradictory leaf boundary would violate the three-layer repair policy and this role's authority.

Stage7 promotion is currently blocked at every layer because no promotion certificate is present or valid for the current evidence contract. Static Stage 6 readiness must not be mistaken for functional closure.

Any certificate that omits checkpoint, stimulus, target-reference, tolerance, testbench, RTL, loader/harness, complete Transformer-block weight-consumption, exact wrapper, simulator, or tool hashes could permit contaminated evidence reuse. Such a certificate must validate as current_contract_valid=false.

A manifest or DDR image alone cannot prove that the DUT consumed required weights. Missing executed loader transactions or tensor-to-DUT binding coverage is a verifier or harness failure, not hardware correctness evidence.

Dynamic liveness, numeric value, data order, transfer count, AXI protocol, DDR address, and runtime-memory consistency remain pending real-tool obligations. They are downstream gates, not current Stage 6 failures.

If board-interface discovery identifies multiple plausible wrappers, simulation source sets, clocks, modules, or app-shell targets, guessing would break canonical board identity. Bounded approval is required before proceeding.

Resolving clock_target_mhz=0 by an arbitrary value could create a mismatch between pipeline assumptions, sample-project constraints, and implementation timing. The value must come from cited board/project evidence or an approved design decision.

A higher-layer failure must not trigger broad lower-layer reopening without a contradicting boundary trace. Conversely, a trace that invalidates a lower-layer certificate must create a scoped trust barrier and backtrack request before repair.

Verifier capability failures, missing golden-reference generation, or incomplete trace instrumentation must be repaired as checker/harness capabilities. They must not be reported as a DUT hardware pass or patched by changing golden outputs or tolerance.

split_reason: The verification gate DAG spans three distinct repair-loop layers with independently auditable contracts: operator-leaf semantic closure, connected single-layer closure, and board AXI/DDR functional closure. The third layer also requires specialized stream/liveness and memory/runtime review, while a final evidence-gate auditor must reconcile dependencies and ensure Vivado bitstream and board runtime remain downstream. These bounded specialties add value in parallel. SACG memory truth reports no active retry, backtrack, or contamination blocker, so this is refinement of the current ready artifact rather than recovery.
